messages.body: In the beginning was the Prompt

we will be building a self-recursive massively multiplayer harness like codex or claude code but for bigger teams

for example, imagine a startup with two founders, a sales person, two programmers, a designer and a product manager. they will all be able to write prompts in a shared company chat space like slack or discord

bigger particle channels: #sales, #product, #eng
smaller per-team channels: #particle, #project-titan, etc.

particle "projects" will be a thread in one of the channels. a thread/project will be started by a human or agent. once a project is started, a planner agent comes in and executes a prompt like this "come up with a detailed execution plan for the user's prompt, split it into parallelizable tasks". then implementer agents will pick up the work. afterwards a reviewer will review adversarially and post comments, either approving or asking for changes. then the work will go back to the implementers and so on until a fixed point is reached.

the backend will be git-based. the overall org chat workspace attaches to a git repo. each particle project is a ref (not a normal branch but a special reserved branch for particle projects). it's important that users/agents can't overwrite each other's work so figure out a way for git to merge "commits" to these "particle project refs", kinda like a CRDT. this also adds integrity to each project

there will be a google cloud vm runtime in rust called particle worker which will execute all the turns and spawn agents etc. for phase 1 though, we just need an npm run dev setup

any questions? any suggestions? come up with a very detailed execution plan for this, where phase 1 one is just the bootstrap where particle can get started with an npm run particle-worker, and from there on, execute the rest the phases.

split everything into mutually parallelizable tasks that can be executed by separate agents.

for each task, create a detailed plan to that a junior engineer could execute it
projects/threads can also be kicked off from github issues (#github-issues) - this being the first one. for this we'll need a github app
this repo will be the "host" repo for itself. so particle projects will create PRs and project refs on this very repo
Q1 - the UI is like Slack, not Slack itself. I just used the example to illustrate how this works. You can reference #2 for more detailed UI/UX and chat there as well
Q2 - at first we'll use codex oauthed. basically "bring your own harness" to codex - research how this works usually
Q3 - yes, public is fine. just remember not to be too embarassing or leak anything from personal machines :)

Q4 - yes
Q5 - MIT
Q6 - tbd, ask me when necessary

suggestions
determinism as core invariant - ok
dogfood on github - for as long as necessary and not longer
yes on merge authority
ULIDs yes. use something like prj_1N3jzjKN2a
